text:
marta_oncall: Heads up — node gpu-ccr-12 in us-west1 just kernel-panic'd and I see repeated ECC corrections followed by an oops. Auto-drain kicked in.
nodewatcher-bot: [automated] Detected 5 ECC_CORRECTED errors then kernel panic on instance gpu-ccr-12. Initiating cordon+drain.
alex_dev: On it, pulling logs. Is this affecting active hosted API capacity?
marta_oncall: Yes, we're seeing queueing spikes on the us-west1 model tier. 2X latency for a handful of routes.
emma_sre: Can we shift traffic to us-west2 or to the dedicated pool? What's the remaining headroom?
ajob: (quick note) // this is a stray placeholder message to mimic quick typo
alex_dev: Noted. Looking at cluster: us-west1 GPU pool at 78% alloc, reserved/dedicated at 88% — limited headroom. We can failover low-priority routes to us-west2, but some enterprise customers pinned to us-west1.
marta_oncall: For pinned customers we should try live-migrate only non-pinned shards. Start failover plan A: 1) cordon & drain node 2) migrate preemptible workloads off 3) shift non-pinned traffic to us-west2 4) if capacity still degraded, spin up a temporary replacement in the dedicated pool.
alex_dev: Executing drain commands now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-ccr-12
kubectl drain gpu-ccr-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
alex_dev: Draining succeeded for 18 pods, 3 pending because of local storage — taking manual eviction on those.
josh_hw: I'm joining — based on ECC pattern could be a GPU memory module starting to fail. I'll open a hardware ticket and request RMA with the colo provider.
emma_sre: Can we toggle caching or increase batching to reduce QPS temporarily? Might buy time without adding infra cost.
marta_oncall: Yes, set batching to +25% for affected models, and enable prefix caching for known hot prompts. I'll update the runtime policy.
nodewatcher-bot: [automated] Traffic shift initiated: 35% of non-pinned routes -> us-west2.
alex_dev: After shift, 95th latency for generation routes back down to baseline for non-pinned. Pinned customers still seeing some degradation but within SLO margins for now.
josh_hw: Vendor ticket created: TKT-449812. Report: GPU ECC corrected errors escalating to kernel panic. Requesting onsite diagnostics and component swap. ETA for tech is 6 hours.
emma_sre: If ETA is >4h we should consider spinning a hot-replacement GPU instance in the dedicated pool for the pinned tenants. Cost check: estimated burn ~ $450/hr while active. Approve?
marta_oncall: Approve for now. Prioritize customer SLAs. Keep replacement up until provider confirms stable hardware.
alex_dev: Spun up replacement instance in dedicated-gpu-pool, migrated pinned pods. Command: `kubectl --context=prod set nodeSelector ...` (applied). Confirmed pods scheduled successfully.
nodewatcher-bot: [automated] Replacement instance gpu-ccr-12-repl registered and passed health checks.
emma_sre: Monitoring: 5xx errors dropped to baseline, latency stable. Cost alert to finance flagged at +$2k for the week if we keep dedicated replacement running.
josh_hw: I'll coordinate RMA and ask for a spare GPU swap. If onsite tech can replace within 6h we'll decommission repl when original is back online and tested.
marta_oncall: Action items: josh to manage RMA, alex to keep pods migrated and monitor perf, emma to watch costs and throttle if burn > $3k wk, I'll update incident channel and customers.
alex_dev: Also dumping kernel oops to ticket:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, PID 2345
[ 1234.567891] Memory ECC error corrected
[ 1234.567892] show_stack+0x4c/0x80
[ 1234.567893] gpu_reset: panic
```
cloud-support-bot: Support case opened with colo: CS-99821. Requested expedited RMA.
josh_hw: Colo confirmed next-available tech for 5.5 hours, but local team said they may arrive earlier. Keeping repl until tested.
emma_sre: I'll prepare a cost amortization note and notify growth/finance. Also adding an autoscale suggestion: add one pre-warmed spare in us-west1 for critical pools to avoid customer pinning collapse next time.
marta_oncall: Good idea. For now, keep everyone updated in #incidents. I'll mark this thread as ongoing and will post resolution when RMA completes and original node passes memtest. :white_check_mark:
